title: 3D Printing and Additive Manufacturing
text: 3D printing, or additive manufacturing, is a process of creating three-dimensional objects from a digital file by depositing successive layers of material. The most common consumer technology is Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM), which extrudes thermoplastic filaments. Other technologies include Stereolithography (SLA, using UV resin), Selective Laser Sintering (SLS, using powdered materials), and metal 3D printing using selective laser melting. 3D printing was invented by Charles Hull in 1984. Applications span prototyping, aerospace (complex lightweight parts), medicine (prosthetics, implants, bioprinting), architecture, and consumer products. The technology enables complex geometries impossible with traditional subtractive manufacturing methods.
